context.body: After two full years, Absalom had sheep shearers in Baal Hazor, which is beside Ephraim; and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.

observations.body: After two years Absalom stages sheep-shearing, insists Amnon attend, commands servants to kill him, while a false report reaches David and Absalom escapes to Geshur.
observations.label: Absalom kills Amnon and flees: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Absalom, Amnon, David, Jonadab, royal sons, servants, and Talmai, Baal Hazor, Jerusalem, and Geshur, waiting, inviting, commanding, killing, fleeing, reporting, mourning, and longing visible within David's story or later memory.

observations.body: Absalom, Amnon, David, Jonadab, royal sons, servants, and Talmai · Baal Hazor, Jerusalem, and Geshur · waiting, inviting, commanding, killing, fleeing, reporting, mourning, and longing · delayed vengeance removes one son and sends another into exile

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 13:23–39 as its own taking, rebuke, and house fracture David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places delayed vengeance removes one son and sends another into exile inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
